title: On Determining the Convergence Rate of an Infinite Product of Stochastic Matrices
summary: By a convergent set is meant a set of stochastic matrices where every infinite product of matrices from every compact subset converges to a rank one matrix. Well-known examples include the set of all scrambling matrices, the set of all stochastic matrices with all diagonal entries positive and a rooted graph, the set of all Sarymsakov matrices, and the set of doubly stochastic matrices with positive diagonal entries and a weakly connected graph.
